anchor.surface_text: CIVIL APPELLATE JURISDICTION Civil Appeal No. 25 of 1954. Appeal by Special Leave granted by the Supreme Court of India by its Order dated the 11th December, 1953, from the Judgment and Order dated the 16th November, 1953, of the Election Tribunal, Cuttack, in Election Case No. 4 of 1952.

facts.text: Election Tribunal Cuttack set aside election of appellant to Legislative Assembly Orissa from Kendrapara Constituency

anchor.surface_text: This is an appeal by special leave against the order of the Election Tribunal, Cuttack, setting aside the election of the appellant to the Legislative Assembly, Orissa, from the Kendrapara Constituency.

facts.text: Four persons including appellant and respondents 1 to 3 nominated for election to Kendrapara seat

anchor.surface_text: Four persons, the appellant and respondents Nos. 1 to 3, were duly nominated for election to the seat.

facts.text: Loknath Das third respondent withdrew candidature leaving contest to three candidates

anchor.surface_text: One of them, Loknath Das the third respondent herein , withdrew his candidature, leaving the contest to the other three.

facts.text: Election held between 9th and 15th January 1952 appellant secured largest votes declared elected

anchor.surface_text: At the election which was held between 9th and 15th January, 1952, the appellant secured the largest number of votes and was declared elected.

facts.text: Respondent Jadumoni Mangaraj presented petition under section 81 Representation of People Act 1951 alleging corrupt practices by appellant

anchor.surface_text: The respondent Jadumoni Mangaraj, then presented a petition under section 81 of the Representation of the people Act No. XLIII of 1951 alleging various corrupt practices on the part of the appellant, and praying that the election might be set aside.

facts.text: Last date for presenting petition was 4th April 1952

anchor.surface_text: The last date for presenting the petition was 4th April, 1952.

facts.text: Petition delivered at post office Cuttack on 3rd April 1952 for registered post reached Election Commission Delhi on 5th April 1952

anchor.surface_text: It was delivered at the post office at Cuttack on 3rd April, 1952, for being sent by registered post, and actually reached the Election Commission at Delhi on 5th April, 1952, a day beyond the period prescribed.

facts.text: Petition defective in verification not specifying paragraphs verified on personal knowledge vs information

anchor.surface_text: It was also defective in its verification. Section 83 (1) of the Act enacts that the petition should be verified in the manner laid down in the Civil Procedure Code for the verification of the pleadings. facts.text: Election Commission condoned delay in presentation on 2nd July 1952

anchor.surface_text: On 2nd July, 1952, the Election Commission passed an order condoning the delay in the presentation of the petition.

facts.text: Election Commission on 3rd July 1952 drew attention to verification defect suggested apply to Tribunal for amendment

anchor.surface_text: By another communication, dated 3rd July, 1952, it drew the attention of the petitioner to the defect in the verification, and suggested that he might apply to the Tribunal for amending it.

facts.text: Order passed under section 86 appointing Election Tribunal Cuttack on 15th July 1952

anchor.surface_text: On 15th July, 1952 an order was passed under section 86 of the Act appointing the Election Tribunal, Cuttack, for the hearing of the petition.

facts.text: Election Tribunal ordered amendment of verification amended on 24th July 1952

anchor.surface_text: The petitioner then applied to the Election Tribunal for amending the verification. That was ordered, and the verification was amended on 24th July, 1952, so as to conform to the prescriptions laid down in Order VI, rule 15 (2), of the Civil Procedure Code.

facts.text: Election Tribunal by majority held three corrupt practices established against appellant

anchor.surface_text: by its judgment dated 16th November, 1953, it held by a majority that three of the corrupt practices set out in the petition had been established against the appellant.
